title: A Surprise Birthday Party for Grandma
passage:
Next Saturday is Grandma's seventieth birthday, and Tom's family is planning something special. "We are going to throw a surprise party for Grandma," Mom said. "But we must keep it a secret!" Tom felt excited. He had never planned a party before.
On Friday night, everyone got busy. Tom and his sister decorated the living room with colorful balloons and a big banner that said "Happy Birthday!" Dad ordered a chocolate cake, Grandma's favorite flavor. "We have to finish everything before she comes home," Dad reminded them.
Mom called Grandma and said, "Can you come to our house at six o'clock tomorrow? We will have a quiet dinner together." Grandma did not know about the real plan at all.
On Saturday, all the relatives arrived early and hid behind the sofa. At exactly six o'clock, Grandma opened the door. Everyone jumped up and shouted, "Surprise! Happy Birthday!" Grandma was so surprised that she almost dropped her bag. "I can't believe you did all this for me," she said, smiling with tears in her eyes.
They sang songs, ate the delicious cake, and shared old family stories. Grandma said, "This is the best birthday I have ever had. Thank you all so much." Tom felt proud. He realized that planning a party is hard work, but seeing Grandma's happy face made it worth every minute.

Please keep this plan a secret.
Tom felt excited about the surprise party.
Chocolate cake is Grandma's favorite dessert.
Dad reminded them to finish before six o'clock.
All of our relatives came to the party.
The guests arrived early and hid behind the sofa.
Tom realized that planning a party is hard work.
Tom felt proud after the party was a success.

grammar: be going to / will 表示未來計畫或預測：be going to 強調事先安排好的計畫（We are going to throw a party.），will 可表示當下決定或承諾（We will have a quiet dinner together.）。
must 與 have to 表示「必須」：must 常表示說話者主觀認為的必要（We must keep it a secret.），have to 表示客觀上的需要或規定，依主詞變化第三人稱單數用 has to（We have to finish everything. / She has to leave now.）。

reading.q: Whose birthday was the family celebrating?
reading.ex: 文中提到「Next Saturday is Grandma's seventieth birthday」，是慶祝奶奶的七十歲生日。

reading.q: What did Mom say they must do about the party?
reading.ex: Mom 說「But we must keep it a secret!」，表示必須保密。

reading.q: What was Grandma's favorite cake flavor?
reading.ex: 文中提到 Dad ordered a chocolate cake，那是 Grandma's favorite flavor。

reading.q: What did Mom tell Grandma on the phone?
opts: To come at six o'clock for a quiet dinner
reading.ex: Mom 在電話中說「Can you come to our house at six o'clock tomorrow? We will have a quiet dinner together.」

reading.q: How did Grandma react when she opened the door?
reading.ex: 文中提到 Grandma was so surprised that she almost dropped her bag，顯示她非常驚訝。

grammar.q: We ___ throw a surprise party for Grandma next Saturday.
grammar.ex: be going to 用來表示事先安排好的未來計畫，故選 are going to。

grammar.q: We ___ keep it a secret, or Grandma will find out!
grammar.ex: must 表示「必須」，強調說話者認為非常重要的義務。

grammar.q: Dad said, "We ___ finish everything before she comes home."
grammar.ex: have to 表示客觀上必須做的事，後面直接加動詞原形，故選 have to（must to / will to 為錯誤用法）。

grammar.q: Mom said, "We ___ have a quiet dinner together tomorrow."
grammar.ex: will 可用來表示當下所做的承諾或未來的預測，故選 will。

grammar.q: Grandma ___ to leave early tomorrow because of a doctor's appointment.
grammar.ex: 主詞 Grandma 為第三人稱單數，have to 要變成 has to，故選 has。

vocab.ex: surprise 指「出乎意料、令人驚訝的事」。

opts: make it look nicer with decorations
vocab.ex: decorate 意為「裝飾」，使空間看起來更漂亮。

opts: is not told to other people
vocab.ex: secret 指「不讓其他人知道的事」，即秘密。
relative 意為「親戚」，指有血緣或婚姻關係的家人。

vocab.q: If Tom feels "proud" after the party, he feels ___.
opts: satisfied and pleased with what he did
vocab.ex: proud 意為「感到自豪、滿意」，通常因自己做了值得驕傲的事而產生。
